frameTiming.harness: headless Chromium via SwiftShader (software rasteriser, no GPU)
frameTiming.caveat: Absolute frame rates from this harness are a floor, not a prediction for real hardware. Useful for regression detection, not for asserting the 60 FPS budget.

map.notes: Three synchronised planes (imagery / survey / labels). Verified at five zoom levels from planet to street.

fog-of-war.notes: Two-pass WebGL mask: MAX-blended coverage buffer, destination-out composite. Minimum on-screen radius keeps corridors legible when zoomed out.

demo-data.notes: Deterministic 18-month history in the subject's local time. Road-following waypoints; regression tests for impossible journeys, unbacked visit counts and out-of-range timestamps.

exploration.notes: H3 res-9 cells for statistics, continuous stamps for rendering. Accuracy drives reveal radius and strength; flights reveal endpoints only.

routes.notes: 1151 segments collapse to 43 unique routes; travel frequency drives line weight.

statistics.notes: Pure aggregation, 23 tests, ~3ms on the full dataset. Chart excludes flights so one long-haul does not flatten 18 months of daily life.

achievements.notes: 13 achievements; the demo user earns 10. Country attribution inferred from city proximity, with the limitation stated in the UI.

search.notes: 496 indexed entries over user history plus a curated world gazetteer. 0.072ms per query. Results carry exploration state.

gps.notes: Real geolocation with battery profiles. Every documented fault surfaces distinctly; bad fixes are marked excluded, never deleted.

permissions.notes: Insecure context reported separately from denial; mid-session revocation detected.

timeline.notes: 453 days grouped and virtualised. Replay interpolates on real elapsed time, so a stop in a journey visibly pauses.

storage.notes: Lossless GeoJSON and raw JSON export work. IndexedDB persistence is NOT implemented; the demo world lives in memory and the UI says so.

ui.notes: One design system across map HUD, four drawers, search and onboarding.

onboarding.notes: One screen, two honest choices; demo needs no location permission.

privacy.notes: Top-level panel. Home masking and delete-all do real work; deletion returns the map to unexplored.

performance.notes: Frame intervals and heap are now measured (pnpm perf). Memory stability is verified: zero heap growth across two identical interaction passes. The 60 FPS budget remains UNVERIFIED because this environment has no GPU.

places.notes: Places exist in the model and statistics; there is no dedicated places surface or favouriting UI.

openIssues.summary: The 60 FPS budget is still unverified: the headless harness renders via SwiftShader with no GPU, so it can only detect regressions, not confirm the budget. Needs a run on real hardware.
No IndexedDB persistence. Live-tracked fixes are not durable across a reload; only export is implemented.
No discovery animation. Newly revealed territory appears without the 'new territory discovered' moment the brief calls for.
The reveal is rebuilt wholesale; live tracking has no incremental update path.
Subsequence matching is loose — 'tok' matches 'Thessaloniki'. Exact prefixes still rank first.
Revealed imagery reads dark where a narrow corridor crosses dense tree canopy at city zoom.

resolvedIssues: MapLibre stylesheet load order collapsed map containers to zero height.
Fog mask rendered nothing: modelViewProjectionMatrix expects world-pixel coords, not normalised mercator.
Matrix uploads silently rejected because MapLibre supplies Float64Array where uniformMatrix4fv requires Float32Array.
Stencil/scissor state inherited from MapLibre discarded the composite pass.
Radius folded into the corner attribute collapsed the radial falloff.
Duplicate place labels across the fog boundary; fixed with a dedicated label plane.
Demo road trips interpolated straight lines across San Francisco Bay.
380 stacked commute polylines compounded alpha into opaque bands over the map.
MapLibre rejects a zoom expression nested inside a multiply.
Rail stretched to the drawer's width and hid its own buttons behind it.
Demo routine generated in UTC put a San Francisco commute at 03:45 local.
Local-time generation dated the tail of the history after its declared end.
Place.visitCount was inflated relative to the visit records backing it.
Performance was entirely unmeasured; frame timing and heap instrumentation now exist and show no per-frame retention.
nextUp: Confirm the 60 FPS budget on real GPU hardware.
IndexedDB persistence so live tracking survives a reload.
Discovery animation for newly revealed territory.
